subject: Data retention exception follow-up / FinFlow discovery
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@finflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (data retention / PII)

Hi Olivia — thanks for your time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we have aligned expectations on data handling and retention: 

Key takeaways:
- FinFlow priority: 0-retention for PII-bearing end-user content in production (no persistent storage of prompt/response pairs).
- Fraud and analytics needs: you need short-lived operational logs for anomaly detection (recommended window: 7–30 days).
- Data residency: EU for EU customers; US for US customers — must support regional isolation and export controls.
- Auditability: you want an auditable trail for security events (longer retention possible if logs are hashed/pseudonymized).

Open items / asks we committed to: 
1) Internal proposal from Redwood on a narrow exception that supports 0-retention for PII content while allowing shortened encrypted logs for operational debugging/fraud. Rafael to outline technical approach.
2) Draft retention schedule and SOW language for your legal team to review (Camila / Marissa to produce).
3) Share SOC2 + penetration test summary and the security questionnaire you mentioned (Olivia to send).

Next steps (timelines):
- Today: Olivia to send the security questionnaire and any sample retention requirements.
- Mon 28 Jun: Redwood to send a short proposal (retention schedule + technical controls) and an example SOW redline.
- Early next week: quick sync if needed with FinFlow legal to close the exception.

If that all looks right, I’ll get Rafael and Marissa to draft the proposal and loop in Neha for legal language.

Thanks again,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0122

Attachment: FinFlow_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (received during call?)

From: Olivia Chen <olivia@finflow.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: FinFlow Legal <legal@finflow.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (data retention / PII)

Hi Camila — thanks for the clear notes and timeline. Two clarifications from legal/ops: 

1) When we say 0-retention for PII we mean no plaintext retention of any field that could identify a natural person (names, emails, SSN, account numbers). We are open to short-lived (<=7 days) operational logs if they are encrypted and access-controlled, and only used for fraud detection/incident response.
2) For analytics we can accept aggregated metrics only; we cannot accept re-identifiable logs beyond that 7-day window.

I've attached the security questionnaire (FinFlow_Security_Questionnaire.pdf) and a short spreadsheet listing our retention requirements for different data types (see FinFlow_req_list.xlsx). Our legal team asked for SOW language that explicitly lists the retention windows and the region of processing.

Can your team produce a simple table with proposed retention per data type and the controls (encryption-at-rest, access roles, purge automation)? If so we can move to a redline quickly.

Best,
Olivia
Head of Product Ops, FinFlow
olivia@finflow.com
(555) 212-4470

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap + next steps (data retention / PII)

Hi team — drafting a concise proposal for FinFlow. High-level recommendation below (will turn into a one-page table and attach):

Proposed retention schedule (initial draft):
- End-user prompt/response content: 0-retention (no persistent storage in production). Ephemeral KV cache only for in-flight requests; KV purge on completion.
- Operational logs (IP blocks, request metadata, non-PII telemetry): retain for 7 days, then purge. Logs are encrypted with customer-specific KEK and rotated.
- Security/audit logs (auth events, admin actions): retain for 90 days in EU region for regulatory auditing; can be pseudonymized (hashed identifiers) on export.
- Aggregated analytics (usage metrics, model latency histograms): retained 24 months unless FinFlow requests shorter window.

Technical controls to include: encrypted-at-rest with per-customer keys (KMS integration), role-based access controls, automated retention/purge jobs with immutable audit trail, and explicit export controls to keep EU data in EU. Rafael — can you add a short note on how we implement 0-retention for PII while still enabling short-lived debugging traces?

I’m attaching the draft retention proposal and a sample SOW snippet. If Neha could review the SOW language for legal phrasing we’ll send to FinFlow by EOD.

Attachment: retention-proposal-v1.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@finflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap + next steps (data retention / PII)

Hi Olivia — appreciate the quick reply and the attachments. That’s very clear and matches what we heard in the call. Next steps from our side: 

- We will send a one-page retention table + short SOW redline by EOD today. That will include: explicit 0-retention language for PII prompt/response, 7-day encrypted operational log retention, 90-day pseudonymized audit logs in-region, and the controls you asked for (KMS, RBAC, purge automation).
- Rafael will add a short technical appendix describing how we provide ephemeral debugging traces without persisting PII (traces are only available to named engineers for a limited time and are purged).
- Neha will prepare the legal clause options (two variants: 0-retention guaranteed vs. target with limited exception for incident response).

Would you prefer we send the SOW as a Google Doc (for collaborative redline) or a PDF redline? Also, can you confirm the contact at FinFlow legal we should loop in? I’ll include both options and call out which clause would be needed for 0-retention (hard guarantee) vs. an exception path.

If all good, we’ll send the materials and schedule a 30-minute sync with legal later this week.

Best,
Camila

--
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0122
